# northflank_combined_service (Resource)

Manages a Northflank combined service: it builds one branch of a Git repository and runs the result, redeploying on every new commit unless `disable_ci` is set. For builds without a running service, use `northflank_build_service`.

`build_arguments` and `runtime_environment` values are stored in Terraform state. Treat the state file as a secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "northflank_project" "app" {
  name   = "My Application"
  region = "europe-west"
}

# Builds main with buildpacks and runs it, redeploying on every push.
resource "northflank_combined_service" "web" {
  project_id      = northflank_project.app.id
  name            = "Web"
  deployment_plan = "nf-compute-20"
  instances       = 2

  repository = {
    url      = "https://github.com/acme/web"
    provider = "github"
  }
  branch = "main"

  build = {
    buildpack = {
      build_context = "/web"
    }
  }

  command = "npm start"

  # Scale on a queue-depth gauge the app serves on /metrics.
  autoscaling = {
    min_replicas = 1
    max_replicas = 5
    custom_metrics = {
      path = "/metrics"
      port = 9090
      metrics = [
        { name = "queue_depth", type = "gauge", threshold = 100 },
      ]
    }
  }

  ports = [
    { name = "http", internal_port = 3000, protocol = "HTTP", public = true },
  ]

  health_checks = [
    {
      type                  = "readinessProbe"
      protocol              = "HTTP"
      path                  = "/"
      port                  = 3000
      initial_delay_seconds = 10
      period_seconds        = 10
      timeout_seconds       = 2
      failure_threshold     = 3
    },
  ]

  runtime_environment = {
    PORT = "3000"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `branch` (String) Branch of `repository` to build and deploy.
- `build` (Attributes) How the code is built. Set exactly one of `dockerfile` or `buildpack`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build))
- `deployment_plan` (String) ID of the compute plan each instance uses, such as `nf-compute-20`.
- `name` (String) Name of the service, 3 to 54 characters. Changing this forces a new service, since Northflank derives the `id` from it and cannot rename one.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the service belongs to. Changing this forces a new service.
- `repository` (Attributes) Git repository to build from. Northflank reaches it through a Git account linked to the team in the Northflank dashboard, which this provider does not manage. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--repository))

### Optional

- `architecture` (String) CPU architecture of the service's infrastructure, `arm` or `x86`. For a build service this is the architecture of the images it builds; for a deployment it is the architecture of the nodes it runs on. Left unset, Northflank uses `x86`. Northflank cannot change it, so changing it forces a new service; removing the attribute keeps the current value.
- `autoscaling` (Attributes) Scale the number of instances between `min_replicas` and `max_replicas` based on load. Set at least one trigger; the service scales up when any of them is exceeded. Leave the block out to run a fixed number of `instances`.

While autoscaling is on, the autoscaler owns the instance count, so `instances` is not read back. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling))
- `build_arguments` (Map of String, Sensitive) Build arguments passed to every build, as a map of name to value. Values shared by several services belong in a `northflank_secret_group` with `secret_type` set to `arguments`.
- `build_plan` (String) ID of the compute plan builds run on, such as `nf-compute-200`. Northflank picks one when this is not set.
- `command` (String) Command to run instead of the built image's `CMD`.
- `description` (String) Short description of the service, up to 200 characters. Removing it from configuration keeps the current value.
- `disable_ci` (Boolean) Stop building new commits automatically; builds then only start when triggered. Defaults to `false`.
- `entrypoint` (String) Entrypoint to run instead of the built image's `ENTRYPOINT`.
- `health_checks` (Attributes List) Probes Northflank uses to decide whether an instance is started, alive and ready. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--health_checks))
- `instances` (Number) Number of instances to run. `0` scales the service down without deleting it. Defaults to `1`.
- `ports` (Attributes List) Ports the service listens on, and whether each is reachable from the internet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ports))
- `runtime_environment` (Map of String, Sensitive) Environment variables set on every instance, as a map of name to value. Values shared by several services belong in a `northflank_secret_group`.
- `stage_id` (String) ID of the project environment the service belongs to. Environments are created in the Northflank dashboard. Changing this moves the service. Left unset, a new service goes in the default environment, and an existing one stays where it is; removing the attribute does not move it back.
- `tags` (Set of String) Previously defined Northflank tags to attach to the service.

### Read-Only

- `app_id` (String) Full identifier Northflank uses for the service's deployment.
- `created_at` (String) Creation time, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the service, derived by Northflank from `name`.
- `uid` (String) Permanent identifier of the service. Unlike `id`, it never changes and is never reused.

<a id="nestedatt--build"></a>
### Nested Schema for `build`

Optional:

- `buildpack` (Attributes) Build with Cloud Native Buildpacks, without a Dockerfile. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build--buildpack))
- `dockerfile` (Attributes) Build with a Dockerfile from the repository. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--build--dockerfile))

<a id="nestedatt--build--buildpack"></a>
### Nested Schema for `build.buildpack`

Optional:

- `build_context` (String) Directory in the repository to build. Defaults to `/`.
- `builder` (String) Buildpack stack. Defaults to `HEROKU_24`.
- `buildpacks` (List of String) Custom buildpacks to use instead of the stack's defaults, in order.
- `storage_size` (Number) Ephemeral disk for each build, in MB: `16384` (16 GB), `32768`, `65536`, `131072`, `262144` or `524288`. Northflank picks its default when this is not set; which sizes are available may depend on the plan.
- `use_cache` (Boolean) Cache build dependencies between builds. Defaults to `false`.


<a id="nestedatt--build--dockerfile"></a>
### Nested Schema for `build.dockerfile`

Optional:

- `build_engine` (String) `buildkit` or `kaniko`. Defaults to `buildkit`.
- `cache_storage_size` (Number) Persistent disk for the layer cache, in MB, such as `16384` (16 GB). It holds the cache and the running build's scratch space; Northflank prunes the cache at about 60% full. Builds that run in your own cluster need it for `use_cache`, and are rejected with "Internal cache storage is required when using internal cache" without it. Only applies to the `buildkit` engine.
- `path` (String) Path of the Dockerfile in the repository. Defaults to `/Dockerfile`.
- `storage_size` (Number) Ephemeral disk for each build, in MB: `16384` (16 GB), `32768`, `65536`, `131072`, `262144` or `524288`. Northflank picks its default when this is not set; which sizes are available may depend on the plan.
- `target` (String) Stage to build, for a multi-stage Dockerfile.
- `use_cache` (Boolean) Keep build layers in persistent storage between builds. Only applies to the `buildkit` engine. Defaults to `false`.
- `work_dir` (String) Build context directory in the repository. Defaults to `/`.



<a id="nestedatt--repository"></a>
### Nested Schema for `repository`

Required:

- `provider` (String) Git provider hosting the repository: `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `azure`, `self-hosted` or `origin`.
- `url` (String) URL of the repository, such as `https://github.com/acme/api`.

Optional:

- `account_login` (String) Login of the linked Git account to use, when several accounts of the same provider are linked. Northflank picks one with access otherwise.
- `self_hosted_vcs_id` (String) ID of the self-hosted Git server, when `provider` is `self-hosted`.
- `vcs_link_id` (String) ID of the linked Git account to use, as an alternative to `account_login`.


<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling`

Required:

- `max_replicas` (Number) Most instances to run. Must not be below `min_replicas`.
- `min_replicas` (Number) Fewest instances to run, at least 1.

Optional:

- `cpu_threshold_percentage` (Number) Scale up when average CPU usage exceeds this percentage of the plan, 10 to 100.
- `custom_metrics` (Attributes) Scale on Prometheus metrics the service exposes itself. The API cannot switch this trigger off without its settings, so removing the block stops sending it; should Northflank keep it anyway, the next plan shows it as a difference. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling--custom_metrics))
- `memory_threshold_percentage` (Number) Scale up when average memory usage exceeds this percentage of the plan, 10 to 100.
- `requests_per_second_threshold` (Number) Scale up when requests per second per instance exceed this value.

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling--custom_metrics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling.custom_metrics`

Required:

- `metrics` (Attributes List) Metrics to scale on. At least one is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling--custom_metrics--metrics))
- `path` (String) Path the metrics are served on, such as `/metrics`.
- `port` (Number) Port the metrics are served on.

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling--custom_metrics--metrics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling.custom_metrics.metrics`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the metric, as exposed.
- `threshold` (Number) Scale up when the average across instances exceeds this value.
- `type` (String) `gauge`, used as is, or `counter`, used as a rate per second.




<a id="nestedatt--health_checks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `health_checks`

Required:

- `failure_threshold` (Number) Failed checks in a row before the instance counts as failing, 1 to 255.
- `initial_delay_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait before the first check, 1 to 1800.
- `period_seconds` (Number) Seconds between checks, 10 to 600.
- `protocol` (String) `HTTP` (needs `path` and `port`), `TCP` (needs `port`) or `CMD` (needs `cmd`).
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait for a response, 1 to 60.
- `type` (String) `livenessProbe`, `readinessProbe` or `startupProbe`.

Optional:

- `cmd` (String) Command to run inside the container.
- `path` (String) HTTP path to request, such as `/healthz`.
- `port` (Number) Port to check.
- `success_threshold` (Number) Successful checks in a row before the instance counts as ready, 1 to 255. Only for a `readinessProbe`: Northflank rejects it on other probe types.


<a id="nestedatt--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ports`

Required:

- `internal_port` (Number) Port number the container listens on.
- `name` (String) Name identifying the port, up to 8 characters.
- `protocol` (String) `HTTP`, `HTTP/2`, `TCP` or `UDP`. Only HTTP ports can be public.

Optional:

- `disable_nf_domain` (Boolean) Stop routing the port's default `code.run` domain, so that it is reachable only through `domains`. For public HTTP ports with custom domains. Defaults to `false`.
- `domains` (Set of String) Custom domains routed to this port. Each must already be verified in Northflank.
- `public` (Boolean) Whether the port is exposed to the internet. Defaults to `false`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Combined services are imported as <project_id>/<service_id>.
terraform import northflank_combined_service.web my-application/web
```
